correctness.rationale: The observed Gaussian score is derived by conditioning X on Y; the null resample scores are iid standard normal after division by ||Y||, so the Monte Carlo exceedance count is conditionally binomial. Uniform rank gives exact null size. The local fixed-B limit follows from chi concentration. On reciprocal exact-size budgets, rejection is comparison with a beta uniform order statistic; its variance and the explicit second derivative of the alternative tail function yield the stated coefficient. The embedded standard-library replay checks the numerical values and asymptotic scaling.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text inspection shows that the primary asymptotic CRT power paper deliberately takes the empirical resample count to infinity, while the original CRT paper emphasizes resampling cost and Monte Carlo uncertainty. Targeted semantic and literature searches did not locate the finite-B Gaussian power identity, fixed-B local limit, or first-order resampling tax. The accepted novelty claim is therefore narrow and retains a generic-randomization-literature residual risk.
residual_risks: Older Monte Carlo randomization or permutation-test literature may contain a generic order-statistic power expansion that specializes to the same coefficient without using CRT terminology.
The coefficient is stated only on exact-size reciprocal-level subsequences; off-subsequence lattice corrections can dominate the same order.

value.rationale: CRT resampling cost is a documented bottleneck. The claim converts that computational budget into exact statistical power for a canonical Gaussian model and shows a persistent fixed-B local-power loss plus an explicit 1/B correction. The 5% h=2 example shows a practically material gap at the minimum feasible budget, so this is a motivated design fact rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
